 Emirates NBA Cup: Live updates, scores and where to watch for Friday’s action
 The Pacers beat the Knicks 106-104 as they earned their first victory in Group Play.
 Jerry Jiang, for NBA.com
 Updated on November 14, 2026 3:34 AM The Pacers beat the Knicks 106-104 as they earned their first victory in Group Play.
 Emirates NBA Cup Group Play continues Friday, headlined by a Prime Video doubleheader featuring the Knicks visiting the Pacers ( 7 ET ) and the Spurs hosting the Warriors ( 9:30 ET ).  
 Follow along for live scores, highlights and updates from around the league.
 What we know about Emirates NBA Cup group play, Nov. 13
 Friday’s action tips off with the Indiana Pacers hosting the New York Knicks ( 7 ET, Prime Video ), followed by the Golden State Warriors facing the San Antonio Spurs ( 9:30 ET, Prime Video ).  
 The Indiana Pacers beat the New York Knicks 106-104 to earn their first win in Emirates NBA Cup Group Play. All five starters scored in double figures.  
 Yaxel Lendeborg and the Golden State Warriors have won eight of their last nine games as they face Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs, who ride a 10-game win streak. 
 The Warriors will be without Stephen Curry with an oblique tear . However, Lendeborg has stepped up. In the previous game vs. the Houston Rockets, Lendeborg had another double-double: 25 points and 10 rebounds.  
 The Spurs are heading into Friday’s action with a historic 10-game win streak, as they join the 2017-18 Boston Celtics as the only teams in NBA history to win 10 straight games after starting a season 0-2. That Celtics team won 16 straight after starting 0-2. Can the Spurs replicate that? 
 Check out Emirates NBA Cup standings.  
 10:30 PM / NOV. 13 
 Why Run Plays When You Have Wemby?
 Warriors 22, Spurs 45. 6:47, 2Q .  
 The Warriors found some offensive life with an 8-0 run.  
 Then, Castle found Wembanyama for the slam, ending that stretch for the Warriors.  
 Wembanyama is averaging 5.2 dunks per game. There’s no need to run plays when you have Wembanyama on the floor.  
10:17 PM / NOV. 13 
 The Largest Spurs’ Run In The Play-By-Play Era
 Warriors 14, Spurs 38. End 1Q.   
 The Spurs’ 18-0 run is their largest run to open a game in the play-by-play era.  
 Check out the entire run uncut here.  
 18-0 SPURS RUN TO START THE GAME, UNCUT 💨
 IT'S THEIR LARGEST RUN TO OPEN A GAME IN THE PLAY-BY-PLAY ERA! pic.twitter.com/0nt6piSDlg 
 — NBA (@NBA) November 14, 2026 
10:03 PM / NOV. 13 
 Warriors Seeking Offense As Spurs Roll
 Spurs 26, Warriors 8. 3:25, 1Q .  
 The Warriors are starting to find some offense as LJ Cryer has 6 points and Gui Santos broke the seal.  
 Meanwhile, Castle has 13 early points and has made all 3 of his 3-pointers. 
 Oh, and Victor Wembanyama is doing Victor Wembanyama things too.
 WEMBY REVERSE SLAM TO CAP OFF AN 18-0 RUN FOR THE SPURS 😲
 SAN ANTONIO IS SIZZLING ON PRIME! pic.twitter.com/IGPj5J8SDM 
 — NBA (@NBA) November 14, 2026 
9:49 PM / NOV. 13 
 12-0 Start For The Spurs
 Warriors 0, Spurs 12. 9:33, 1Q.   
 Victor Wembanyama is doing it all to start the game, as he’s already dished out 3 assists. 
 The Spurs have shot 5-for-6 from the field. Stephon Castle has 6 points early.  
9:45 PM / NOV. 13 
 Pacers Escape With Cup Win
 Knicks 104, Pacers 106. Final .  
 After Siakam missed two free throws that would’ve put the game away, the Knicks rushed back and put themselves in a position to come back after Mikal Bridges cut the Pacers’ lead to 2.  
 The Knicks get a critical stop after forcing the Pacers to a turnover.  
 But with a chance to send the game to overtime, Towns missed the go-ahead jumper and the Pacers survived. 
 The Pacers go 1-1 in Group Play and the Emirates NBA Cup defending champions go 0-2.  
 PACERS HOLD ON FOR THE EAST GROUP B WIN IN A THRILLER! pic.twitter.com/y3SOxZAl7E 
 — NBA (@NBA) November 14, 2026 
9:32 PM / NOV. 13  
 Yaxel’s Rise Gives The Warriors New Life
 Warriors vs. Spurs. Pregame .  
 Heading into this season, the Golden State Warriors were without Jimmy Butler, Moses Moody and Kristaps Porziņgis, who later announced he was stepping away from basketball.  
 After losing their first three games, things were looking bleak. Then, the Warriors rattled off eight straight wins. 
 Stephen Curry, who will miss the next two weeks due to his oblique injury, was the main catalyst in the surge. 
 But another surprise came along: rookie Yaxel Lendeborg.   
 Some rookies look to start their careers in stride, but for Lendeborg, he has high expectations.  
 “I’m trying to be an All-Star this year,” Lendeborg told Amazon Prime’s Taylor Rooks. “I want to be the young guy that changes the whole persona of the team.”  
 It’s safe to say that through his early career, Lendeborg has done that by injecting new life into the Warriors. He’s averaging 21.7 ppg, 7.4 rpg and 3.7 apg through 12 games.  
 The Warriors are 1-1 without Curry this season. In a 124-112 win over the LA Clippers, a game that Curry missed, Lendeborg recorded his career-high 37 points. That was the highest-scoring performance by a Warriors rookie since Curry’s 42 points in 2010.  
 Now, Lendeborg and the Warriors look to snap the Spurs’ 10-game win streak after having their own 8-game win streak snapped the game before.  
 "I want to be the young guy that changes the whole persona of the team."
 Yaxel Lendeborg wants to make a big impact in his first season with the Warriors 🌉
 🍿 GSW/SAS
📺 9:30pm/et, Prime https://t.co/tV9bvmxv1m 
 — NBA (@NBA) November 14, 2026 
9:23 PM / NOV. 13  
 Pacers Barrage
 Knicks 89, Pacers 99. 7:42, 4Q .  
 Every time the Knicks find some rhythm, the Pacers fight back with a run of their own.  
 Five Pacers starters are up to double-digit scoring, led by Siakam’s 17 points. Ivica Zubac has a double-double with 12 points and 12 rebounds.  
 They’re in the midst of a 12-2 run.  
 9:16 PM / NOV. 13 
 Franz Heat Check
 Bucks 84, Magic 94. 4:29, 4Q .  
 Franz Wagner recorded his fourth consecutive game with 30+ PTS, marking the longest such streak of his career. He now has 33 points and counting as the Magic are in cruise control.  
 He’s also recorded his first triple-double of his career with 10 rebounds and 11 assists.
 9:13 PM / NOV. 13 
 Giannis Eurosteps His Way To A Major Dunk
 Cavaliers 57, Heat 54. End 1H .  
 What do you do when you see Giannis Antetokounmpo flying at full speed with bad intentions at the rim?  
 You would probably concede the dunk, as there’s no defense for that. Well, the Cavs did just that, as there was no defense for him.  
 Giannis is up to 17 points and 7 rebounds, but the Heat trail heading into the second half.  
 GIANNIS EUROS INTO A POSTER SLAM 😲 pic.twitter.com/q54CDeBW0J 
 — NBA (@NBA) November 14, 2026 
8:58 PM / NOV. 13 
 The Brunson Burner Is Alive
 Knicks 84, Pacers 85. End 3Q .  
 The Knicks continue to show their fight as they are on a 13-2 run over the last 2 minutes. 
 Brunson creates space with his nifty footwork and drills the bucket for 27 points on the night. He also has nine assists.  
 The Knicks end the 3Q with a 15-4 run. They trim Indiana’s lead to 1.  
 8:57 PM / NOV. 13  
 Rise Up, Jerami Grant!
 Grizzlies 48, Pelicans 45. 5:31, 2Q .  
 Ty Jerome finds a rolling Jerami Grant, who throws it down with authority.  
 Grant has 7 points as the Grizzlies and Pelicans battle in West Group B.  
 JERAMI GRANT ONE-HAND SLAM 💥 pic.twitter.com/Ru94gafoO8 
 — NBA (@NBA) November 14, 2026 
 8:54 PM / NOV. 13 
 Count It For 4 For Desmond Bane
 Bucks 75, Magic 87. 9:49, 4Q .  
 Desmond Bane is dangerous in transition with his shooting, as demonstrated here.  
 Bane finds the range on the 3-pointer and gets the foul as well. Bane notches 21 points, and he joins Wagner (27) as the Magic players who have scored 20+ points.  
 The Magic are leading comfortably in the third.  
 DESMOND BANE 4-POINT PLAY 🔥
 He's up to 21 PTS (13 in Q3)! pic.twitter.com/PELThygdv1 
 — NBA (@NBA) November 14, 2026 
 8:52 PM / NOV. 13 
 Spida Gets Tricky With This Dime
 Cavaliers 41, Heat 43. 6:16, 2Q .  
 Although he initially gets on the ground after losing the ball, Donovan “Spida” Mitchell somehow gets the ball over to Tyrese Proctor, who nails the 3-pointer.  
 After this bucket, Proctor has 12 points as the Cavaliers try to come back in the game. 
 SPIDA FINDS PROCTOR FROM THE GROUND 🎯
 Tyrese Proctor has 12 PTS (3 3PM) in Q1! pic.twitter.com/oNbe4acMHA 
 — NBA (@NBA) November 14, 2026 
8:43 PM / NOV. 13 
 History For Buddy Hield
 Hawks 31, Bulls 46. 9:05, 2Q. 
 Buddy Hield has always been a great 3-point shooter throughout his career. Whether it’s with the Sacramento Kings, the Indiana Pacers, the Golden State Warriors or now with the Chicago Bulls, Hield will give you 3’s when you need them.  
 His best season shooting the 3-pointer was in the 2017-18 season with the Sacramento Kings, where he shot 43.1% from distance.  
 On Friday, he made history as Hield passed Kyle Lowry for 14th on the All-Time 3-point made list. Next up is Jamal Crawford at No. 13. 
8:42 / NOV. 13 
 Pacers Playing At Their Pace
 Knicks 60, Pacers 65. 8:45, 3Q.   
 Whenever a coach calls a timeout when the game, half or quarter just started, it’s usually not a good sign. 
 After Oubre nailed a 3-pointer, Mike Brown didn’t like what he saw and immediately called a timeout. Since then, the Knicks have woken up and rallied off 8 straight points, cutting the Pacers’ lead to 5.  
 KAT also made history as he recorded his 12th consecutive double-double to start the season, surpassing Willis Reed (11) for the second-longest streak in Knicks franchise history. He now trails Walt Bellamy (13).  
8:16 PM / NOV. 13 
 Pacers Playing At Their Pace
 Knicks 49, Pacers 58. End 1H.   
 It’s been a back-and-forth battle, but the Pacers have taken control heading into halftime with a nine-point lead.  
 Pascal Siakam is leading the way with 13 points and the Pacers are utilizing all of their most of  their bench with 11 players suiting up already. They’re shooting 41.6% from the field and 40% from the 3-point range.  
 The Knicks are led by their star-studded duo Karl-Anthony Towns and Jalen Brunson, who have 14 and 13 points so far, respectively. Towns is one rebound shy of notching his 12th straight double-double.  
 Across 11 regular seasons since joining the Knicks, Brunson is averaging 30 ppg while shooting 49.4% from the field. With the Knicks surging as of late, they’ll need Brunson and KAT to heat up in the second half to continue their strong play. 
 As for the Pacers, they’ve found success going to Siakam’s efficient play. Who else will step up to get the Pacers back on track?
7:52 PM / NOV. 13 
 Franz Continues Hot Start   
 Magic 34, Bucks 27. 5:34, 2Q .  
 Franz Wagner dropped 38 points in a 123-108 win over the Utah Jazz on Wednesday, tying a career high. 
 Wagner is continuing his blistering shooting. He’s up to 14 points and has already drilled 2 3-pointers while shooting 5-for-7 from the field.  
7:42 PM / NOV. 13 
 No Love Lost Between These Two Teams
 Knicks 38, Pacers 35. 7:26, 2Q .  
 The Knicks and Pacers have a storied history. As Eastern Conference rivals, the Knicks lead the overall series 115-97, but the Pacers lead 30-24 in playoff games and overall series wins (6-3).  
 Since 1993, these two teams have met in the playoffs nine times.  
 In their most recent playoff matchup in the 2025 Playoffs, Tyrese Haliburton and the Pacers came back from a 17-point deficit in Game 1, with an homage to Reggie Miller’s infamous celebration back in their 1995 series.  
 Right now, Karl-Anthony Towns is leading the Knicks as he’s up to 14 points, 12 of which came from the first quarter.
 KAT SCORED 12 PTS IN Q1 👏
 Knicks lead the Pacers on Prime! pic.twitter.com/QfhypIRVwX 
 — NBA (@NBA) November 14, 2026 
7:31 PM / NOV. 13 
 Jay Huff, The Rare 3-D Center
 Knicks 23, Pacers 24. 1:41 
 When the Pacers inserted Jay Huff, he inserted some energy to the game.  
 He scored 8 points in 4 minutes of action, with 2 3’s. Stan Van Gundy called him a “3-and-D center,” which is fascinating since that term is usually reserved for wings.  
 The Pacers are shooting 50% from the field as the pace (no pun intended) has picked up. 
7:20 PM / NOV. 13 
 Knicks Are Starting To Groove Early
 Knicks 16, Pacers 9. 7:39, 1Q   
 The Knicks are starting to look like their championship selves, zipping the ball with crisp passes and early transition buckets.  
 Through the first 11 games, the Knicks have been one of the slowest teams in the NBA in terms of pace, which was the direct opposite of the formula that worked for their championship run.  
 However, the Knicks are rolling early, with slick passes from Jalen Brunson and Josh Hart leading to easy buckets. The Knicks have made their last seven shots and their second 7-0 run of the game.  
 The Knicks have won six of their last eight games. Can they continue this good stretch?  
5:00 PM / NOV. 13
